rationale: B is clearer. It tracks the frame state as it goes, in a few documented fields (frame, rollInFrame, pinsDown), and Roll updates that state with an easy-to-follow branch for frames 1-9 and a small switch for the tenth frame. Its Score is a uniform three-case loop that also scores the tenth frame correctly without special-casing. A instead re-derives the whole game state from scratch on every roll and every score call, in a long frameState function with many early returns and nested tenth-frame logic that is hard to verify. Its Score also adds tenth-frame branches that are not needed. B's only blemish is a minor gofmt misalignment in its error var block. Overall B is simpler, easier to reason about and more idiomatic.
